key_insight: Human hearing appears to vary continuously across a five-dimensional space rather than falling into fixed audiogram “types.”
clinical_relevance: A coordinate-based hearing map could improve how clinicians track subtle within-ear changes and support more precise otology research, genetics, and trial design.
method: Analyzed 4.29 million audiograms from 33 datasets across 8 countries and 62 years.
Reconstructed unseen audiograms and compared patterns across calibration standards.
Tested whether reported hearing “types” were real or artifacts of quantization and pooling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-decibel-accurate reconstruction of unseen audiograms and preservation of clinical detail across millions of measurements.
watch_item: This is a large retrospective, multi-dataset modeling study, so real-world adoption will need external validation and careful attention to dataset/calibration differences.
paper_title: The Human Hearing Atlas: a canonical map of human hearing
